title: Construction Spending — Value of Construction Put in Place (March 2027 data), 10:00 a.m. ET — the same minute as ISM Manufacturing
source: EST: cadence arithmetic, re-derived independently on 2026-09-09 from seven Census release calendars fetched direct (calendar-listview-2020…2026.html, all HTTP 200; 1,135 rows parsed, 84 Construction Spending rows across 81 unique release dates). THREE forward-looking schedules were checked and NONE reaches May 2027, which is why this is EST: and not CENSUS: — (1) census.gov/economic-indicators/calendar-listview-2027.html returns HTTP 200 (76,349 bytes) but carries NO indicator table at all (0 <tr> rows, 3,773 characters of body text); (2) the C30 program's own construction/c30/release.html (HTTP 200, 48,117 bytes) ends at its final row 'October | December 1 | 10:00 a.m.'; (3) the Atlanta Fed's GDPNowcastDataReleaseDates.xlsx (HTTP 200, 16,944 bytes) ends at 2026-12-23 with zero 2027 rows. What the record does establish is the rule the date rests on: 75 of 81 Construction Spending releases since 2020 landed on the month's FIRST BUSINESS DAY, and 5 of the 6 exceptions are the post-lapse catch-up dates (2025-11-17, 2026-01-21, 2026-02-27, 2026-03-23, 2026-05-07) — outside the lapse window the rule holds 75 of 76 (98.7%), the single miss being 2020-01-03. The sub-case this date needs is cleaner still: in the 24 months whose 1st fell on a weekend, the release moved to the next business day 21 of 21 times outside the lapse window (Monday, or Tuesday where Monday was a federal holiday). The exact calendar geometry recurs — May 1 last fell on a Saturday in 2021, and the March-2021-data edition released Monday 2021-05-03. 2027-05-01 is a Saturday, 2027-05-02 a Sunday, 2027-05-03 a Monday with no federal holiday (Memorial Day is 2027-05-31) and a normal NYSE session. Filed estimate on three counts, all load-bearing: no Census primary publishes a 2027 schedule, this lane may not self-confirm an event discovered in-sweep, and the post-backlog recovery is seven editions old (2026-06-01 through 2026-12-01, every one of them that month's first business day), not a decade. Discovered 2026-09-09 by the never-assessed initial research of ism-manufacturing-2027-05-03; canonical file written 2026-09-09 by this event's own initial research after reading the single proposal
notes: Canonical file written by this event's initial research (2026-09-09) after reading the one proposal, `construction-spending-2027-05-03.from-ism-manufacturing-2027-05-03.json`, now shadowed. The proposal's headline claim — that the 2026 backlog created a natural experiment on the same-minute ISM confound, because for several months the two prints did NOT share a session — HAS NOW BEEN RUN AND IS SPENT. The control set is exactly 9 first-business-day sessions where ISM printed at 10:00 without Construction Spending (2020-01-02, 2025-10-01, 2025-11-03, 2025-12-01, 2026-01-02, 2026-02-02, 2026-03-02, 2026-04-01, 2026-05-01) against 72 with. Every one of eight comparisons points the same way but none separates: SPY session range 1.111% vs 0.858% (p=0.35), XHB 2.164% vs 1.807% (p=0.30), ITB 2.244% vs 2.022% (p=0.42), QQQ p=0.49; normalising each session against its own surrounding 43-session window SHRINKS the gap further (SPY percentile 0.643 vs 0.548, p=0.69; XHB 0.595 vs 0.500, p=0.53), so even the direction is partly a quiet-window artifact — the 9 controls are drawn from one contiguous post-lapse window at a median VIX of 16.99 against 18.94. And a bootstrap power run settles it: at n=9 the design reaches 80% power only if removing this print HALVES XHB's session range, and catches a 40% cut on SPY just 39% of the time. The window closed when cadence resumed 2026-06-01, so n cannot grow without another shutdown. The ISM-slot confound is permanently unresolvable on this calendar's data — future sessions should stop reserving the test. The distinguishing feature of THIS edition is its reference month: March carries the largest raw seasonal load of the year (+10.94% median NSA m/m since 2015, roughly double the next month), and the year-to-year dispersion in its implied seasonal factor (sd 0.85pp) is on its own about 3x the median headline m/m this report prints (0.30%) and slightly above Census's own median stated margin of error (±0.80%). Impact LOW and `symbols: []` match the three existing construction-spending entries; no house playbook is macro-keyed (0 hits, re-grepped 2026-09-09). Proposed and kept as an estimate; nothing here licenses an entry. Ledger: docs/research/events/construction-spending-2027-05-03.md
